corpus_scope_statement: Training uses a deterministic bounded subset of at most 10,000 documents per source (40,000 before deduplication), not the entire 4.5-billion-token corpus.

architecture_record.substantive_difference_from_submission01: six-layer bidirectional encoder plus six-layer causal decoder with encoder-decoder cross-attention
architecture_record.student_design_rationale: A 512-wide 6+6 pre-norm Transformer stays above the 50M parameter floor while remaining practical on a 16 GB Kaggle GPU. Training uses 512/256-token pairs, while 1024/512 positional limits provide safer inference headroom. The bidirectional encoder can form a full-prompt legal representation, and every decoder block can retrieve it through cross-attention while preserving causal target prediction.

innovation_hypothesis: Compared with the Submission 01 decoder-only baseline, a bidirectional encoder feeding a causal decoder through cross-attention is expected to improve use of long-range facts, parties, provisions, and procedural context in legal continuation. The comparison will use held-out token cross-entropy/perplexity, BERTScore F1, ROUGE-L F1, BLEU-4, and declared repetition diagnostics. The frozen Submission 01 BPE mapping, bounded official corpus, deterministic split, source mixture, scratch training requirement, and evaluation protocol remain controlled; this is a pre-training hypothesis, not a conclusion.
ablation_control: Submission 01 decoder-only baseline under a matched data/tokenizer/evaluation protocol
